short: Co–Fe–Cr (oxy)Hydroxides as Efficient Oxygen Evolution React
title: Co–Fe–Cr (oxy)Hydroxides as Efficient Oxygen Evolution Reaction Catalysts

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Efficient, earth-abundant catalysts are needed to lower the OER overpotential. Ternary Co-Fe-Cr (oxy)hydroxide of suitable composition should give dense, more active high-valence Co sites.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/modification), n5 (DES/variable_sweep), n6 (PRC/synthesis), n16a (PRC/treatment). Premises: Co2+/Co3+ sites in Co (oxy)hydroxides undergo PCET to Co4+, which completes the OER cycle

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Co5Fe3Cr2 (oxy)hydroxide is low-crystalline (near-amorphous). Cr incorporation drives Co into octahedral sites in Co5Fe3Cr2 and Co5Cr5.
states.detail: Absorbed: n7 (STR/phase/fraction), n9 (STR/phase/site_occupancy), n9b (STR/phase/site_occupancy), n10 (STR/chemistry/composition), n10b (STR/chemistry/composition), n16b (STR/phase/identity). Premises: Cr2+ preferentially sits in fourfold (tetrahedral or square-planar) coordination; Co L3/L2 edge ratio is a Co valence descriptor: lower ratio = higher valence (Co(OH)2 4.36, CoOOH 2.74)

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Fe-Cr synergy lowers Co2+->Co3+->Co4+ energies so Co3+delta active sites form at lower anodic potential. Co5Fe3Cr2 is the optimum composition, with the smallest eta10 (232 mV) in 1 M KOH.
states.detail: Absorbed: n11 (MEC/pathway), n12 (PRP/value), n16c (PRP/value), n17 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Co L3/L2 edge ratio is a Co valence descriptor: lower ratio = higher valence (Co(OH)2 4.36, CoOOH 2.74)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Co5Fe3Cr2 holds ~1.52 V at 50 mA cm-2 for 7 days in 1 M KOH. Co5Fe3Cr2 reaches eta10 = 452 mV in neutral 0.5 M KHCO3, better than IrO2 and the other catalysts

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Fe-Cr co-substitution in amorphous Co (oxy)hydroxide tunes Co valence/coordination, giving an active, stable OER catalyst

nodes.title: evidence, F3

nodes.note: at.% values only in text text says Fe-containing samples have HIGHER L3/L2 ratios; the inset shows them LOWER, which (per k2 and F5b references) is what higher Co valence implies
